title: Mushroom Stroganoff
subtitle: Rich creamy mushroom stroganoff served over rice or pasta
excerpt: Chestnut and portobello mushrooms cooked with onion, garlic, smoked paprika, and a generous amount of soured cream. Ready in 25 minutes. A satisfying meatless main.

recipe.sourceNotes: Beef stroganoff, named after the Russian Stroganov family, is a dish of sautéed beef in a soured cream sauce. The mushroom version became a popular vegetarian alternative in British cooking during the 1980s and 1990s, using large meaty mushrooms to provide the same satisfying texture. The key flavourings are the same: smoked paprika, a good slug of brandy or sherry if using, and soured cream added at the end so it does not split.

recipeTools.notes: A wide pan gives the mushrooms room to colour rather than steam.

content.text: Cook the mushrooms in a very hot, dry pan first to drive off the moisture before adding the butter. Wet mushrooms release water and stew rather than fry. Add the soured cream off the heat: heat splits it. Season at the end as the soy sauce and cream are already salty.

Heat a large frying pan over very high heat without any oil. Add all the mushrooms and cook for 4 to 5 minutes without stirring, until they colour. They will release then reabsorb their liquid. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the butter and onion. Cook for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Return the mushrooms to the pan. Add the mustard and soy sauce. Stir to combine. Remove from the heat.
Stir in the soured cream off the heat. Season with salt and pepper. Scatter with parsley. Serve over rice, tagliatelle, or mashed potato.
